page.layout: One printed page. A single text block with Latin and Arabic lines, and marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at top: page number left, title "NOTÆ." centred. No headings, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: (inquit AlSharestanius ) الذين غلوا في حق أبدهم[?] حتى أخرجوهم من حدود الخلقية وحكموا فيهم باحكام الالهية Qui in antistitibus suis celebrandis adeo modum excesserunt ut ipsos extra rerum creatarum terminos evexerint, & divinas ipsis proprietates attribuerint. Utrimque autem transgressi sunt, dum & hominum ἀνθρώπων[?] statuerunt, & in Deo corporeitatem asseruerunt. Sic enim pergit ille, فردوا[?] شبهوا واحدا من الائمة بالالهة وربما شبهوا الالهة بالخلق وهم على طرف الغلو والتقصرc.de الغالية alias autem assimilarunt Antistitum aliquem Deo, aliàs Deum creatura. atque ita in utroque peccant extremo excessus & defectus. Variae sunt & horum sectae, & variae in diversis regionibus appellationes. Fuit ex illis Abdolla Ebn Saba (quem Judæum fuisse perhibent, atque idem in Judaismo de Josua filio Nun prædicasse) qui Alim salutaret انت انت Tu es Tu, i.e. انت الاله Tu es Deus, & ab hoc اشعبت اصناف الغلاة divisæ sunt species eorum qui modum excesserunt, quorum alii idem aut ejusmodi alia de Ali, alii de aliquo ex ipsius posteris affirmarent, & mortuum eum fuisse negarent, rediturúmque olim in nubibus, terramque justitia impleturum. Inter posteros ipsius magni apud suos nominis fuit Mohammed quidam. de quo hoc idem asseruerunt asseclæ ipsius, adeo ut ipsius reditum inter fidei articulos numeraverint. Atque hinc forsan error ille apud nostros quo vulgo creditur Mohammedistas Prophetæ sui reditum expe-AlSharest. c.de الختاردة[?]ctare

page.notes: Left margin also shows a dot (not text) and a faint stain at the left edge (not transcribed). A faint watermark at the bottom right is a digitiser's mark and is omitted. Arabic lines are read from a small, slightly blurred scan: "أبدهم", "فردوا", the word after "داخل" in the Arabic line with "ديه", and the second "اتت" in the Arabic of "Tu es Tu" are uncertain and marked [?]. The Greek word after "hominum" is uncertain and marked [?]. Long s printed as f in "Jofua", "fuiffe", "falutaret" is transcribed as s. The second marginal note beside "qui Alim" reads "c.de السيا" with "ديه" below it, possibly part of the same note; kept as one note with its Arabic text.
